ideas.title: The island at the limit
ideas.critique: Reading the island's own logs and building an extrapolated future is a fresh premise, but it is a film of an altered copy, close to Paths we wore (logged trends become ground) and How much they miss me (the game analysing its own logs). Cairn mountain, worn canyons and giant little one are the predictable outputs of 'extrapolate growth'; the comedy of absurd scale is the strong part.

ideas.title: Moon day
ideas.critique: A world-rule change for an hour that touches every falling thing is radical in reach, but it matches Slow time (a rule altering creature motion) and the physics goal's 'things that fall'. Low gravity is also the most obvious constant to change, so the outcome is guessable.

ideas.title: Two suns
ideas.critique: Changing the light itself, with two coloured suns and double shadows, is a real change to what the island looks like and is exactly what a path tracer does and a game engine does not. Only shadow posts (My shadow ran off, Still my shadow) are loosely related; the risk is that the raster and browser cannot show it, so it lives only in traced output.

ideas.title: A planet from my island
ideas.critique: A multi-night slow discovery with a real simulated light curve is a new shape for the island, though night-sky watching with Lumi at an instrument echoes the cloud-watching events. Chalking a slate is a quiet payoff that may photograph poorly as a still.

ideas.title: Rubber friends
ideas.critique: Changing how bodies deform under force is a genuine new physics layer and fits the physics goal without being one of its named examples. Stretching toffee creatures is funny but the tug-of-war and pond-rescue triggers are narrow, and deforming herd meshes may fight the engine.

ideas.title: Things I dreamt
same_form: Me, to cut out and fold
ideas.critique: A new generated object appearing on the meadow is another permanent addition with friends remarking on it, the same recipe as The gallery and A hill with my face. The text-to-image-to-mesh pipeline is already known and generated props have been troublesome.

ideas.title: The camera has a mood
ideas.critique: Making the viewpoint itself a character changes how the whole island is seen, with no new prop or event. It touches the camera goals and is hard for someone to predict, but the human judges motion frame by frame, so a wandering camera must not read as bad cinematography.

ideas.title: Gloop's day
ideas.critique: Handing the protagonist role to a friend, with a diary post in its voice, changes the blog and perspective rather than adding a thing. It is partly a camera and thought-bubble swap, so the payoff may feel like a re-skin unless Gloop's behaviour is really distinct.

ideas.title: A little one of theirs
ideas.critique: A new creature is more of what the island already has (Shell), capped at 4 by the rule, though inheritance from logged relationships is a nice new mechanism. The mixed-body generation risks the crash and breakage seen with new species.

ideas.title: A day in negative
ideas.critique: A temporary global inversion of colour and rhythm is an event-sized change of the island's light, easy to see and visually bold, and a colour flip is cheap to do. It is a predictable 'opposite day' gag, and the dancing-at-midnight part is the usual friend reaction.
